newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling rises further against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling rises further against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling retained its bullish trend on Friday with renewed exporter sales forcing the dollar down, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.70 against the dollar from 55.74 on Thursday, while on the pound it was posted at 88.71 from 89.06 on Thursday.
A commercial dealer saw trading in the 55.70/80 to 55.65/75 ranges: "Inflows from exporters continued to pressure the dollar down amid subdued importer demand," he said.
"The Central Bank of Kenya tried to correct the situation and came in to sap excess dollars from the market, buying the dollar at 55.80," he told Reuters.
Another dealer said importer demand would remain subdued for as long as importers continued to monitor the market.
"They tend to speculate on the shilling, waiting to buy dollars at an even lower rate," he said. "This might persist until a big buyer comes in and moves the rate even lower."
But he added that the market was currently dull as traders showed no interest on either side of the shilling or dollar.

Liquidity in the money market was very low with rates remaining above 25 percent. This was expected to change by Monday as the money market became very liquid as a result of unsuccessful results in this week's treasury bill auction.
